title: Questions for the reader
rule: Beside each panel a paper hand points to a printed question for the reader ('Where is the key now?'); the answers run upside down at the foot.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p54_questions_for_you.py (cards and felt: p28_dealt_cards.py, which imports 99-ways-subjective/test-shot-build/lightbox.py and e4.py)
made: six lit paper cards laid square on the lightbox felt board (page 28's first-person cards, rebuilt: the 99-ways-subjective lamp-lit fibrous sheet, set pieces cut sharp, the agent's own scissor-cut paper hands soft behind the sheet): memo in his hand; the stranger beyond the TICKET OFFICE glass; the clock at 4:10 with his pencil hand; she turns from the window; his hand swings the cupboard leaf open on the left jamb, the ANRC 1922 key cutout on its hook tagged SERVICE; the key still on its hook, the SERVICE door shut, the pencil coming up

under each card a strip of the same lit paper with a numbered question for the reader in the shared pen hand, and behind it a paper pointing hand: the 99-ways-subjective RightHand rig (scissor-cut sleeve, cuff, forearm, palm, curled fingers, two-segment index and thumb) posed with the index straight and the thumb tucked, reaching in from the left to point at the question
the six answers printed on a long lit strip, numbered, turned through 180 degrees along the foot of the board
the four canon lines on the cards' cut-paper pen-hand balloons; folio '54 / Questions for the reader' (pen99.folio)
questions: 1. What is he to do at 4:15, and where is the key?
2. Who is at the glass, and what does she want?
3. What time does the clock say?
4. Does she stay at the window?
6. Will he open the SERVICE door?
answers: 1. Open the SERVICE door; key in the cupboard.
2. The stranger; she wants the time.
6. No. He has forgotten why he came.

events.E0: card 1: the memo '4:15 - open SERVICE door. Key in cupboard.' in his hand; Q1
events.E1: card 2: the stranger beyond the glass, question balloon; Q2
events.E2: card 3: the clock at 4:10, his answer balloon tailed to the viewer; Q3
events.E3: card 4: she turns from the window, thanks balloon; Q4
events.E4: card 5: the cupboard opened on its left jamb, the key on its hook tagged SERVICE; Q5
events.E5: card 6: the forgetting balloon; key on its hook, SERVICE door shut; Q6

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the paper hands come in one by one, each pointing at its question as it is printed; last, the answers strip is laid upside down at the foot
beat_frames: b01: six cards on the felt, six blank lit strips
b08: the upside-down answers laid at the foot (= the page)

self_check.check: A reader answers each question from the panels alone (each answer is on its own card: the memo text, the balloon, the clock face, the turned figure, the key on its hook, the closed door), then turns the page to check the answers (maker's judgement; blind reading pending)

weaknesses: the six cards are page 28's cards re-laid (same compositions), so the pictures repeat that page; the new work is the strips, hands and answers
the pointing hands are small soft silhouettes behind the strips (the hand rig's thumb sits up like a cocked thumb rather than tucked flat)
the upside-down answers are small print (cap 26 px), legible at full size, tiny at phone width, as answer keys usually are
first-person cards: the agent is never seen, so Q1 (what is he to do) leans on the memo text in his hand
